html:
English nurse and reformer, born in 1820 in Florence, Italy. She founded modern nursing and used statistics to make hospitals cleaner and safer.

Her wealthy family opposed her wish to nurse, which was then seen as low work. In 1854, during the Crimean War, the government sent her with a team of nurses to the British army hospital at Scutari, across from Istanbul. She found filth, crowding and more soldiers dying of disease than of wounds. She pushed for cleaning, food and supplies, and her night rounds made her "the Lady with the Lamp" in the British press.

Her greater work came after the war. She gathered death figures and showed them in clear diagrams, among the first uses of graphics to argue for reform. They helped change army medicine and public health in Britain and India.

In 1860 she founded a nursing school at St Thomas' Hospital in London, which made nursing a trained profession for women. International Nurses Day falls on her birthday, 12 May.
sum: English nurse and reformer, born in 1820 in Florence, Italy. She founded modern nursing and used statistics to make hospitals cleaner and safer.
